turns.user: Can we buy the 5-litre gaskets from a supplier that doesn't have a food-grade certificate? Their price is much better.
turns.agent:
**No, we cannot.** 

According to **Purchase Policy §6.2 (POL-PUR-001 §6.2)** and **Supplier Policy §4.1 (POL-SUP-003 §4.1)**:
* Parts that come into contact with food—including gaskets (item `GSK-SIL-05L` is marked as `food_contact: true` in the item master)—may **only** be purchased from a supplier holding a **valid food-grade certificate** on file in Bahi.
* The certificate must be uploaded and verified before any order can be placed. Even if their price is better, orders cannot be placed with a supplier lacking this certification.

clauses.text: 4.1 A supplier of any part that comes into contact with food (gaskets, lids, body blanks, and any item marked food-contact in the item master) must hold a food-grade certificate. This is the certificate referred to in Purchase Policy §6.2.

clauses.heading: 6. Supplier qualification
clauses.text: 6.2 **Parts that come into contact with food** (gaskets, lids, body blanks and any other item marked food-contact in the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a **valid food-grade certificate** on file in Bahi. The certificate must be uploaded and checked **before the first order** is placed. An expired certificate counts as no certificate.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.5 An expired certificate counts as no certificate. The supplier stays ACTIVE in the master, but no food-contact part may be ordered from it until a new certificate is uploaded and checked.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.2 The certificate must be a test report from a laboratory accredited for food-contact materials (for example an FSSAI-notified laboratory), or a BIS conformity certificate for stainless steel grade 304 or better.
